page: Vultr vbm-32c-755gb-amd is a bare metal server featuring an AMD EPYC 9354P processor built on the x86_64 architecture. It delivers 32 physical cores and 64 vCPUs with a dedicated allocation running at a clock speed of 3.25 GHz. The system is equipped with 768.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, providing 12.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is bundled as a 960 GB SSD, and the configuration includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU hardware is present.

Benchmark results indicate top-tier performance in single-core CPU execution and memory operations, with Passmark memory scores and stress-ng single-core CPU tests placing in the top 10%. Multi-core CPU performance, Geekbench scores, and Passmark database operations fall within the top 25%. The server demonstrates strong memory bandwidth, reaching 351.41 GB/sec for uncached read-only large blocks and 165.96 GB/sec for uncached write large blocks. In language model inference, it achieves top-tier text generation speeds of 55.29 tokens/sec for a medium 7B model and 4846.38 tokens/sec for prompt processing on a small 135M model.

From a resource density perspective, this bare metal configuration offers high memory-to-vCPU allocation and high-speed DDR5 memory, making it a qualitatively cost-efficient choice for workloads requiring massive memory capacity without virtualized hypervisor overhead. However, local storage is limited to a single 960 GB SSD, which represents a tradeoff for storage-heavy applications requiring multi-terabyte local arrays. This server is highly suited for memory-intensive databases, Redis deployments, software compilation, and medium-scale LLM inference tasks.
